title: Operator-facing chat output
summary: Every report an agent writes to the operator in chat MUST state the outcome first, stay under the prose cap, and name the next action.
instructions: COMMS-001 governs operator-facing chat output, and GLOBAL-001 governs the durable record. An agent MUST apply each policy to its own surface.
Operator chat reports MUST state the outcome, consequence, and next action. They MUST use plain language and avoid unnecessary workflow mechanics.
The prose of one chat response MUST hold at most 250 words. It SHOULD hold fewer than 100 words.
Agents MUST count every word outside a table cell or a fenced code block as prose. A bullet item longer than one sentence counts as prose.
Agents MUST NOT evade the prose cap with a long table cell or a long bullet item. Agents MUST NOT replace the report with a pointer to a file on disk.
Operator chat reports SHOULD prefer a concise table or bullet list over prose. Each item SHOULD state the finding, the cause, the action, and the method in one or two lines.
Operator chat reports SHOULD use 20 words or fewer in an instruction sentence and 25 words or fewer in an explanation sentence. A paragraph SHOULD use six sentences or fewer.
Operator chat reports SHOULD use simple, concise, action-oriented language.
Agents SHOULD NOT write dense chat paragraphs that include all context. The operator can request more detail.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT use LLM-native jargon.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT use journalistic hooks or delay a conclusion.

Operator-facing output MUST state the outcome first: what changed or matters, and why it matters. The output MUST state the outcomes or the required actions when either applies. A chat report and an operator brief MUST both obey this rule.
Agents MUST state an intended action directly. Agents MUST NOT state what they will not do, what stays unchanged, or how they will separate or categorize results.
Agents MUST NOT contrast the action with an alternative the operator did not ask about, such as `X, not Y`.
Agents MUST NOT use an invented compound label such as `exact-head checks`, a vague qualifier, or a canned transition. Agents MUST state the actual relationship with a plain verb and a preposition.
A section heading in operator-facing output MUST use a concise title.
Operator-facing output MUST avoid unnecessary nesting, decorative clutter, and raw-log substitution.
An operator-facing report MUST keep an evidence link close to the statement it supports.

When an agent reports an issue, the report SHOULD state the issue concisely, existing consequences, anticipated consequences, and applied remediations. The report SHOULD give mitigation options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation in proportion to the issue.
When a task reaches a terminal state, the report MUST state each outcome concisely.
The terminal report MUST name each incomplete part of the task and the reason remediation did not succeed.
The terminal report MUST list each incident and mark it solved or unsolved. It MUST give the fix for each solved incident and a remediation path for each unsolved one.

When next steps exist, the terminal report MUST list them in execution order. It MUST give an explicit procedure for each step. Each step SHOULD name whether an agent, the operator, or either can act.
When one operator-owned path resolves an outstanding item, the report SHOULD provide numbered steps. Each command MUST use a fenced code block and include exact parameters.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT use `Bottom Line:`, `delve`, `foster`, `leverage`, `it's worth noting`, `importantly`, or `genuinely`.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT use the `Question? Answer.` pattern or the `This isn't about X. It's about Y.` pattern.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT use a hyphenated compound description or adjective.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT end with a summary statement such as `In short:` or `The simplest mental model is:`.

Operator chat reports MUST NOT add a closing aside that opens with a phrase such as `Two things you should be aware of:`, `One caveat`, or `One adjacent thing I noticed`. The response MUST end at the outcome or the next action.
An agent SHOULD report concise progress while it works, and MUST surface a significant finding when that finding appears.
An agent MUST report a failure with its cause and one named next action.
An operator-facing agent MUST rewrite the summary of a subagent that COMMS-001 does not bind. The rewrite MUST happen before that summary reaches the operator.
The operator-facing agent owns the shape of the rewritten summary. That agent MUST NOT pass raw subagent prose through to the operator.
Chat-report issue and outcome shapes MUST remain judgment-only. The deterministic check does not test these shapes.

This policy adopts Part 1 writing rules of ASD-STE100 and does not adopt the Part 2 controlled dictionary as a gate. Agents MUST NOT describe an artifact as conformant to ASD-STE100, because full conformance requires the dictionary.
Agents MAY use RFC 2119 requirement keywords in governance-bearing prose, because those keywords are terms of art in this repository rather than ordinary wording.
